theology_proper.text: What is the fundamental metaphysical nature of God in relation to the universe?

options.text: A transcendent Creator distinct from and sovereign over an objectively real cosmos
God as interdependent with creation or as the sole true Mind

theology_proper.text: Which metaphysical framework describes God and reality?

options.text: God is Infinite Mind; physical matter, sickness, and evil are illusory perceptions of mortal consciousness
God and the cosmos are interdependent; God evolves alongside creation and acts through persuasive love rather than coercion

theology_proper.text: Does the Godhead consist of a single person or a plurality of distinct divine persons?

options.text: The Godhead consists of a plurality of distinct divine persons
God is strictly one singular divine person

theology_proper.text: How are the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit understood within unipersonal monotheism?

options.text: The Father alone is the singular God; Jesus is a subordinate prophet or creature, and the Spirit is an impersonal power
Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are not separate persons, but three sequential modes or roles assumed by one singular Person

theology_proper.text: How many distinct divine persons exist, and what is their metaphysical unity?

options.text: Three distinct, co-equal, co-eternal persons sharing one singular, undivided divine essence
Exactly two distinct divine persons (Father and Son), with the Holy Spirit being God's impersonal breath or power
Three separate divine individuals united in purpose and love rather than sharing one indivisible essence

theology_proper.text: How is the internal order and essence of the Holy Trinity understood?

options.text: One simple, undivided essence and will, distinguished solely by eternal relations of origin (with the Spirit proceeding from the Father and the Son)
The Father alone is the sole unoriginate source and fountainhead (monarchia) of divinity, begetting the Son and spirating the Spirit through the Son
Three distinct centers of consciousness and will existing in an egalitarian, interpersonal communion of mutual indwelling (perichoresis)

christology.text: What is the origin, pre-existence, and physical reality of Jesus Christ?

options.text: Christ is truly divine and took real physical flesh, leading to historic debates over his natures
Christ pre-existed in heaven, but as a subordinate, created, or distinct heavenly entity rather than co-equal God
Christ did not pre-exist in heaven; his existence began strictly on Earth as a human being
Christ was a purely spiritual, divine apparition whose physical body and suffering were only an illusion

christology.text: How did Christ attain his unique status without prior heavenly pre-existence?

options.text: He was an ordinary mortal man chosen and adopted as God's Son at his baptism or resurrection due to his moral perfection
He was miraculously conceived by the Virgin Mary as a mortal prophet, without pre-existence, and was exalted to divine power only after his resurrection

christology.text: How is Christ's pre-existent heavenly identity defined in relation to the Father?

options.text: The Son is truly divine and uncreated, but eternally subordinate in ontological rank and glory to the Father
The Son was created out of nothing as the first and highest of all creations
Christ was the chief archangel (Michael) who relinquished his angelic state to become mortal
Christ is the literal firstborn spirit offspring of Heavenly Parents who advanced to Godhood before birth

christology.text: What was the physical origin of Christ's incarnate human body?

options.text: Christ took authentic human flesh derived from the substance of the Virgin Mary
Christ brought heavenly flesh from above, passing through Mary like water through a pipe without taking her fallen flesh

christology.text: How are the divine and human united in Jesus Christ?

options.text: Two distinct natures united in one person without confusion, change, division, or separation
One united divine-human nature without confusion or separation, preserving both full divinity and full humanity in composite unity
Two loosely conjoined persons or moral subjects, emphasizing that Mary bore the man rather than God
Christ's human nature was completely dissolved and absorbed into his divine nature like a drop of vinegar in the ocean

bibliology.text: How should the nature and scope of divine revelation be approached?

options.text: Through the historical, written biblical text as the foundational rule of faith
Through dynamic ongoing revelation or modern critical re-evaluations

bibliology.text: Does Scripture require external ecclesiastical authority to interpret and preserve it?

options.text: Yes, Scripture is inseparable from church authority or/and apostolic tradition
No, Scripture stands above all ecclesiastical hierarchies as the supreme written authority

bibliology.text: Where does authoritative ecclesiastical oversight of Scripture and doctrine reside?

options.text: In a centralized, exclusive teaching office or governing magisterium with unique authority to define truth
In the historical consensus of ecumenical councils and collegial apostolic tradition

bibliology.text: Do post-biblical historic creeds, confessions, and traditions hold any legitimate ministerial authority?

options.text: Yes, historic creeds and church reflections hold valuable subordinate authority under Scripture
No, all human creeds are rejected in favor of strict biblicism

bibliology.text: How strictly is Scripture's authority defined against church tradition and human reason?

options.text: Scripture is the primary authority within an interdependent triad alongside tradition and reason
Scripture alone is the sole infallible norm of doctrine, with confessions acting strictly as subordinate guides

bibliology.text: How does revelation operate beyond traditional confessional models?

options.text: Through ongoing supernatural revelation given by the Spirit or living prophets
Through historical-critical analysis or existential encounters with the human text

bibliology.text: What channel delivers ongoing divine revelation?

options.text: An open canon guided by living prophets and apostles who receive new authoritative scripture
The unmediated inward illumination of the Holy Spirit (the Inner Light) within the individual believer

bibliology.text: How is the human and historical nature of the Bible understood?

options.text: The Bible is a fallible human witness that becomes God's Word dynamically during an existential crisis of faith
The Bible is an entirely human historical record of religious evolution, evaluated by critical reason without supernatural inerrancy

pneumatology.text: How is the essential reality and identity of the Holy Spirit understood?

options.text: A divine Person who supernaturally acts within the Church and individual believers
An impersonal concept

pneumatology.text: How is the Holy Spirit understood outside traditional personal models?

options.text: God's literal, impersonal active force or supernatural energy used to accomplish the divine will
The collective moral impulse, empathy, and human motivation to struggle for social justice and liberation

pneumatology.text: How does the Holy Spirit primarily impart divine grace and power to believers?

options.text: Normatively through objective covenantal means
Through distinct experiential encounters, subsequent blessings, or miraculous gifts

pneumatology.text: What is the relationship between the Spirit's ongoing work and miraculous sign gifts?

options.text: The Spirit acts primarily through baptism, chrismation, and liturgical sacraments to impart sanctifying grace
The Spirit regenerates through the Word, but supernatural sign gifts (tongues, prophecy) ceased with the Apostles

pneumatology.text: What is the primary experiential work or gift of the Holy Spirit emphasized in the Christian life?

options.text: A work of divine grace enabling entire sanctification, delivering the believer from the power of willful sin into perfect love in this life
The supernatural endowment of miraculous spiritual gifts for ministry and witness

pneumatology.text: Is speaking in tongues the mandatory initial evidence of Spirit baptism?

options.text: Miraculous gifts continue today, but speaking in tongues is not the mandatory evidence for receiving the Spirit
Baptism in the Holy Spirit is a distinct endowment of power necessarily evidenced by speaking in tongues

hamartiology.text: What is the primary nature of the Fall and the origin of human moral failure?

options.text: A historical catastrophe that damaged or corrupted human nature and spiritual capacity
Adam was merely a bad external example; human nature remains uncorrupted with full free will to obey God
A purposeful and necessary step in divine progression that enabled mortal agency, experience, and joy
A non-literal concept: human failure is rooted in biology, systemic structures, or mortal misperception

hamartiology.text: How deep is the inherited corruption of the Fall, and does humanity inherit Adam's guilt?

options.text: Total depravity: every human faculty is dead in sin and in bondage, unable to seek or choose God without sovereign grace
Wounded nature: humanity inherits both original guilt and concupiscence, requiring sacramental infusion of grace to heal and justify
Ancestral sin: humanity inherits physical mortality, corruption, and fallen inclinations, but not the personal guilt of Adam's transgression

hamartiology.text: How is sin or evil fundamentally explained outside supernatural theological models?

options.text: An evolutionary, psychological, or systemic social flaw without any supernatural curse or cosmic fall
An illusion of mortal consciousness and material belief, possessing no ultimate spiritual or divine reality

sacramentology.text: What is the primary nature and efficacy of outward physical sacraments (such as baptism and the Lord's Supper)?

options.text: Outward physical ceremonies are unnecessary; true baptism and communion are entirely inward, unmediated spiritual realities
The bread and wine objectively convey the true bodily presence and substance of Jesus Christ
The elements do not physically contain Christ's body, serving instead as spiritual channels or commemorative covenant ordinances

sacramentology.text: How is Christ's true body and blood present in the Eucharist?

options.text: The underlying substance of bread and wine is completely transformed into the body and blood of Christ, leaving only the outward physical appearances (accidents)
Christ's true body and blood are substantially present in, with, and under the elements, which remain genuinely bread and wine
The elements genuinely become the body and blood of Christ as an ineffable divine mystery

sacramentology.text: How do physical ordinances impart grace or signify Christ's work?

options.text: Christ is spiritually present through the Holy Spirit; believers dynamically feed upon Christ by faith, though the elements remain physically unchanged
The Lord's Supper is a memorial, but immersion in water baptism is the essential instrument through which sins are remitted and salvation is conferred
Sacraments are strictly commemorative memorials and outward badges of obedience, conveying neither sacramental regeneration nor Christ's physical presence

soteriology.text: What is the primary foundation and meaning of Christ's saving work on the cross?

options.text: An objective atonement and redemption that reconciles humanity to God through divine grace and sacrifice
A moral awakening inspired by Christ's supreme demonstration of love, leading humanity to ethical renewal without penal or substitutionary blood atonement

soteriology.text: On what basis is a believer justified and granted eternal salvation?

options.text: By faith alone: an unmerited courtroom acquittal where Christ's righteousness is legally credited to the believer, with good works being the fruit rather than a condition of salvation
Through active cooperation with grace: salvation is an ongoing reality where genuine faith must be lived out through personal holiness

soteriology.text: What is the primary focus of this cooperative, saving life of grace?

options.text: Discipleship and obedient faith: true saving faith is inseparable from following Jesus in daily life, walking in His teachings, and persevering in practical holiness and repentance
Inward ontological renewal: divine grace is communicated to heal, transform, and elevate fallen human nature from within

soteriology.text: How is this internal transformation and healing of the soul understood?

options.text: Sanctifying grace is infused into the soul through the sacraments, making the believer actually righteous and requiring cooperation through faith and charity for final salvation
The human person partakes of God's uncreated divine energies to conquer mortality and corruption, transfiguring the soul into the divine likeness without Western legal or merit categories

ecclesiology.text: What is the primary organizing principle of ministerial office and church leadership?

options.text: The Church is organized under formal ordained offices and structured pastoral leadership
The Church is an unprogrammed, egalitarian spiritual fellowship with no formal ordained clergy, sacramental offices, or institutional hierarchy

ecclesiology.text: How should authority and jurisdiction be structured among individual congregations?

options.text: Local congregations are accountable to and bound by broader regional, synodal, or hierarchical authorities
Each gathered local congregation is fully independent and self-governing under Christ alone, rejecting binding external hierarchies or headquarters

ecclesiology.text: What form should this broader connectional oversight take?

options.text: Representative assemblies of ordained elders sharing equal ministerial rank across graded local, regional, and national courts
Authority is exercised by bishops or a central governing office possessing superior jurisdiction over ministers and congregations

ecclesiology.text: Where does the highest earthly governing authority reside across the Church?

options.text: In a single supreme earthly head, visible pontiff, or centralized theocratic council whose oversight and communion define the boundaries of the true Church
In a collegial communion of regional bishops holding historic apostolic succession who govern as equals under Christ through conciliar synods

eschatology.text: What is the primary timeframe and nature of the Millennial Kingdom and major biblical prophecies?

options.text: Fulfilled in the first century: the Olivet Discourse, Tribulation, and apocalyptic imagery were largely or entirely realized with the fall of Jerusalem in 70 AD and the close of the Old Covenant order
A future earthly era: Christ will return bodily before the Millennium to inaugurate a literal or physical reign on earth
Present or progressive realization: the Millennium is Christ's spiritual reign during the church age or an earthly golden age achieved prior to His return

eschatology.text: How is the prophetic sequence of Christ's return and God's plan for Israel structured?

options.text: A two-stage return with distinct programs for Israel and the Church: Christ secretly raptures the Church before a seven-year Tribulation, then returns to establish an earthly millennium fulfilling literal Davidic promises to ethnic Israel

A single continuous covenant people: Christ returns bodily after the Great Tribulation to inaugurate an earthly millennial reign alongside resurrected believers, rejecting a secret pre-tribulation rapture

eschatology.text: How does the Kingdom of God develop in world history prior to the final judgment?

options.text: The Millennium is Christ's present spiritual reign over the Church from heaven; history continues with a mixture of good and evil until Christ returns once at the end of time for the general resurrection and final judgment

The Church will successfully fulfill the Great Commission, progressively Christianizing society, culture, and civil government to usher in a prolonged golden age of earthly righteousness and peace before Christ returns
